subject: english
question:
**Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No Improvement'.**

He is interested neither in business __or on the__ job.
solution:
The correct answer is: **nor in the.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Replace **'or on the'** with **'nor in the'** to make the sentence correct.
 
• We can use **'neither'** as a conjunction with** 'nor'**. It connects two or more negative alternatives.
 
 
• **Example -** *He likes neither apples nor oranges.*
 
 
 
• So, in the given sentence it will be, **"neither in business nor in the job"**
 
• The meaning of **OR** is used as a function word to indicate an alternative, the equivalent or substitutive character of two words or phrases

Therefore the correct answer is **option 2**.

**Corrected sentence:** *He is interested **neither** in business **nor **in the job.*
